h: Making the most of the market
p: Abingdon Street Market works best when you go with an empty stomach and no fixed plan. Take a lap first to see what all the kitchens are serving, then let everyone pick their own favourite before regrouping at a table. It's a sociable way to eat, especially for groups who can never agree on one restaurant, and it takes the stress out of feeding fussy kids.

The market really comes alive when there's something on. Live music, themed nights and seasonal events pop up through the year, so it's worth seeing what's planned around your visit. Busy evenings can be lively, while daytimes tend to be more relaxed and family friendly.

It's a great base for exploring the town centre too. The Winter Gardens, home to grand ballrooms and theatres, are just around the corner, and the Grand Theatre is a short walk away on Church Street. Blackpool North station is close by if you're arriving by train. Head west to the seafront and you'll reach North Pier and the stretch of Promenade near the Tower, where you can admire the Comedy Carpet and catch a tram along the coast. Shoppers will find the main high street and Houndshill Shopping Centre within easy walking distance, and of course the town's famous amusement arcades are never far away, with some areas being 18+ only. Whether you're grabbing a quick lunch or settling in for an evening, the market's a lovely change of pace from the busy front.
